claims.text: Why even one missed milestone matters: CDC placed each milestone @ the age by which ≥75% of children are expected to show it, so even one missing milestone = “actionable” (likely to prompt screening and poss Refer) and the “wait and see” approach = ↓.
claims.quote: Milestones were placed at ages by which at least 75% of children would be expected to exhibit them, in an effort to make even one missing milestone more "actionable" (likely to prompt screening and possible referral). With a milestone at 50%, half of all children would still reasonably be expected to have not yet achieved it. This change is intended to reduce the "wait and see" approach often taken when a child is missing an average age milestone.

claims.text: ⍉a Screening: the checklist milestones are ⍉develop standards and should ⍉be used as screening or diagnostic tools; if a develop concern = noted, next steps = screening and eval w formal tools, or Refer for services.
claims.quote: The developmental milestones included on CDC's milestone checklists are not developmental guidelines or standards for children's development. They should not be used as screening or diagnostic tools to detect developmental delays. If developmental concerns are noted, the next steps are screening and evaluation with formal tools or referral for services.
